experience.reason: The visceral, cosmic horror established by the Voyd collapses into a cliché, sentimental biological metaphor that feels tonally disjointed and emotionally cheap. It reduces the profound existential stakes of "wanting" to a simplistic, almost domestic image of hunger and warmth, breaking the established atmospheric tension.

The shift to visceral body horror ("ribs are my architecture") feels tonally disjointed from the preceding metaphysical grief, breaking the established thematic cohesion without earning the narrative pivot.

The shift to a visceral, body-horror vignette about a woman and "architecture" feels tonally disjointed from the preceding metaphysical and psychological introspection, breaking the established thematic cohesion. It introduces a confusing new character dynamic that lacks the emotional continuity of the player's personal guilt, causing the narrative momentum to stutter.

The sudden intrusion of the proper noun "Orachys" feels like an unearned expository dump that breaks the intimate, second-person psychological immersion established in previous nodes. It shifts the tone from personal haunting to generic lore-dropping without sufficient narrative justification.
